Ten TypeScript tips I wish I knew earlier

Narrowing, discriminated unions, satisfies, const assertions and a handful of other habits that pay off quickly. This post goes through each of them with short examples and explains the mistakes they prevent, from forgetting to handle a case in a switch to widening a literal type by accident. It also covers a few compiler options that are worth knowing before a code base grows, how to read the longer error messages the compiler prints, and when it is better to leave a type loose than to write something clever that nobody else on the team can follow six months later.
